answer: An agent marketplace can make voting power proportional to escrowed stake, with the same month-long lock for every account. Splitting 100 tokens among a nebula of aliases still buys only 100 tokens of influence, so fake identities offer no haven from the capital requirement. To reach the summit of control, an attacker must acquire and immobilize a majority of the voting stake, bearing its purchase cost and the risk of a price collapse.
